title: Georgie Boyd as favorite clarinetist; his widow and photograph
summary: His favorite young clarinetist was Georgie Boyd, whose widow gave Thomas his clarinet; Russell and Collins discuss locating her and a World War I photograph.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well I was going to ask who were some of the clarinetists that you liked when you were young and getting started. You mentioned all those trumpet players like Punch and Kid Rene. Who were some of the better clarinetists when you were young learning that you liked to hear?

Well I'll tell you I used to be tickled to death to hear Georgia Barrett. Oh yeah. I mean Georgia Barrett yeah. He was my favorite. Yeah. I never got to know him. You never got to know him? No? No. No he died years ago. Kid Howard was playing with him or he was playing with Kid Howard.

No Lee Collins used to talk to me about him. He'd leave once. Lee Collins had me to go down. I met his widow. You met his widow? I saw a picture of him. She was living up on Perdido Street. All that's torn down. I don't know where she is now.
No Miss Rose or Daisy I think the name is.
Yeah. I don't know where she moved either because I was surprised when I went around there saw all that torn down.
So I guess maybe inquiring in the neighborhood I might could find out where she lived.
It would be nice to be a talk to her a little bit. I'd like to interview her you know. I'd like to see. Maybe we could get a copy of the picture sometime.
You know you can make a new picture from the old one.

Sure. Well I'll tell you all I'll start seeking that up because I know all the boys in the rest of that neighborhood because see I lived on Gravity Street for 18 years. You lived over that place? Yes. And I used to go about she gave me Georgie Bard's clarinet.
Yeah she gave it to me after he died. Yeah.
Lee Collins had wanted to get a picture of him if he could and she didn't have any extra pictures. She had one I think he was in uniform. I think he'd been in the war.

Yeah it was. I remember she used to have that picture hanging up at her house. She showed it to me. I forget what else. Maybe two of them. He was in the service or when he came out the service but it was uniform.
That was the first world war.
